editorial:
Imagine being a kid with a plan that is way too big for your age. You meet Ricky, a young boy who is dealing with some heavy stuff after his mom passes away. Instead of just being sad, he is totally focused on one goal: taking out his dad, who is about to get out of prison. It sounds dark, but the movie plays it more like a quirky road trip. Along the way, he runs into Pillier, a salesman who is having a really bad run with life. The chemistry between the grumpy adult and the determined kid creates a vibe that is both funny and a bit sad, making you root for them even when they are doing things they probably shouldn't.

What really makes this work is how the movie balances the laughs with the emotional moments. The acting feels real, and the pacing keeps you interested without dragging. While some parts might feel a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy stories about unlikely friendships, you should definitely check this one out. It is a great pick for a cozy movie night. You can grab the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best quality, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch. It is a hidden gem that deserves more eyes on it.
endingExplained: In the end, Ricky finally comes face to face with his father. Instead of following through with his plan to kill him, the anger and hate he carried start to fade. He realizes that revenge will not bring his mother back or fix his life. The movie wraps up with Ricky finding a sense of peace and a new kind of family in Pillier, choosing forgiveness and friendship over hate.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about unlikely friendships and emotional growth.
